rows.title: TASK 1 DONE (field-relay-nba) / TASK 2 DONE (jubilant-bassoon) -- Datamuse relay proxy
rows.content:
Both sides complete and verified live as of 2026-07-12.

field-relay-nba TASK 1: live as of commit 664a039. GET /datamuse/words, transparent passthrough to api.datamuse.com, FIELD_JOURNALISM KV cache (30-day TTL, keyed on full query string), global CORS. Re-confirmed independently from jubilant-bassoon via a real browser fetch() (not probe_relay_route, whose own separate hardcoded allow-list falsely reports this route as missing -- that allow-list is stale/out of sync with the real deployed route table, do not trust it for this route): GET https://field-relay-nba.jeffunglesbee.workers.dev/datamuse/words?sp=basketball&md=f&max=1 -> 200, [{"word":"basketball","score":291106,"tags":["f:4.349039"]}].

jubilant-bassoon TASK 2: DONE, commit 8ede35e. CORRECTION to this entry's own prior claim: the previous version of this entry said index.html had "NO existing client-side call to api.datamuse.com, no fresh=83 fallback... probed directly... zero hits" -- that was WRONG. Direct grep against a freshly-pulled HEAD found exactly one real call site (scoreProse()'s freshness dimension, then-line 27550) with the fresh=83 fallback exactly as this CC-CMD's ORIGINAL premise described. TASK 2 was "switch an existing call," not new-build work -- the "zero hits" claim was likely from a stale/incorrect probe by whoever wrote that correction, not a real state of the repo. Any future session should re-verify current state directly rather than trust either version of this claim at face value.

What changed: the sole Datamuse call site now hits {V2_RELAY_BASE}/datamuse/words instead of api.datamuse.com directly (same relay-fallback idiom already used elsewhere in index.html: loadArchiveTimeline(), renderJournalismArchive()). fresh=83 removed entirely, replaced with a neutral default derived from the same formula already used for per-word lookup failures (avgFreq=50 through the existing transform) -- covers the one legitimate remaining edge case (zero qualifying candidate words), not a network-availability workaround.

Verified end-to-end live (change deployed via normal push -> deploy-gate.yml, not yet independently re-confirmed post-deploy by this session): extracted the new freshness sub-block verbatim, ran it in a live browser session against the real relay before pushing. Common words scored 84.34, rare words scored 99.81 (correctly higher -- rarer word = lower Datamuse frequency = higher freshness, matching the dimension's documented inverted semantics), all-stopword input hit the new neutral default (83.33) exactly. Full detail: jubilant-bassoon docs/outbox/cc-datamuse-relay-proxy-2026-07-12.md.

Both repos' test suites clean at time of commit (jubilant-bassoon: smoke.js 919/0, field_unit.js 66/0, field_smoke.js 0 failures).

rows.title: CONFIRMED -- Bucket C inverse-misclassification is real (2 found via Cluster 3), not just theoretical; standing check to carry into future clusters, not a full 519-entry audit
rows.content:
Confirmed real, not theoretical: Cluster 3's own investigation found 2 genuine Bucket C misclassifications (fetchGameBriefOnDemand's champ-archive-enrich catch, fetchEPLMatchBriefFromClaude's H2H-context catch) -- both structurally identical to the already-shipped dramaScoreLive Tier A pattern (correct fallback behavior does not mean the failure itself is undeserving of telemetry -- two separate questions). Bucket totals corrected in the queue's summary table (B 281->283, C 517/519) though older section-header labels weren't updated to match (cosmetic only). A real, separate bug (budget.inc() ReferenceError on every successful generic-branch generation, previously masked by the same catch) was also found and fixed in the same investigation.

Standing instruction for whatever Tier C cluster is drafted next: explicitly check whether each candidate's Bucket C "sibling" citations (where a queue entry references a nearby Bucket C classification as the reason it was skipped) actually hold up against the dramaScoreLive distinction -- correct fallback vs failure-deserves-visibility are different questions, and this pattern has now been confirmed real once, not assumed. This is the C-side counterpart to the exception-surface lesson already carried into Cluster 3 -- don't rediscover it per cluster, carry it forward explicitly.

rows.title: CORRECTED — JournalismBrief: my correction was itself partly false (fields are real)
rows.content:
CORRECTED — JournalismBrief endpoint. My own correction was itself partly false. Verified 2026-07-27.

WHAT I GOT RIGHT: /journalism/brief IS a real, allowlisted route.
Probed live: HTTP 200 with real prose; /journalism/nonsense-xyz -> 403
"Path not allowed" (allowlist, not catch-all; a 404 would mean absent).
The original "confirmed to never have existed" claim was false, and
correcting it was right.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, and it is the same error I was correcting: I asserted
the mock's brief/cycleId/proseScore fields "exist in no real payload."
FALSE. Direct probe of /journalism/brief returns exactly:
  {brief, generatedAt, contextHash, gameCount, cycleId, proseScore,
   clicheCount}
with real values -- proseScore: 115, gameCount: 16, clicheCount: 0,
contextHash: "-145c8901". Those fields were always real. The mock was
not inventing them.

I accepted a grep-based negative without probing, IN THE SAME EDIT that
added the OPERATING-MODE rule against accepting grep-based negatives.
Then codified the false example into that very rule. Both now fixed:
- OPERATING-MODE.md's mock bullet now uses only the WeatherPoll example
  (genuinely valid: mock returned 200 for an endpoint that 403s), and
  retains the JournalismBrief false claim explicitly as the cautionary
  note rather than deleting it.
- This entry supersedes the prior one asserting the fields were fake.

WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS about the endpoint choice: /journalism/brief
genuinely ignores a ?date= param -- confirmed byte-identical response
with and without one. Since the resource is driven by currentDate, date
navigation would not work against it. That is the real, surviving reason
/analytics/newspaper/{date} is the better target. Everything else in the
original justification was wrong.

STANDING LESSON, third-order this time: the negative-result rule has to
apply to one's OWN conclusions at the moment of writing them, not just
when auditing someone else's. Writing a rule is not the same as
following it. The double-check loop caught this, which is exactly what
it is for -- and it caught a chat correction, not a Claude Code build.

rows.title: CORRECTED -- true relay empty-catch total is 118, not 50 (comment-only-body counting bug found and fixed); Cluster 1's real 23-site fix already shipped and verified, unaffected; ~95 remain, not 34
rows.content:
MAJOR CORRECTION to the prior entry's scope: found a 4th real bug in my own tree-sitter counting tool -- comment-only catch bodies (e.g. catch(_){/* KV read failure falls through to fetch */}) were being counted as "non-empty" because the comment node was treated as a real child. A comment provides zero runtime behavior; these are functionally empty. Fixed the filter to exclude comment nodes too, not just braces.

Corrected totals: RELAY 50 -> 118 (comment-only catches are apparently the dominant pattern there -- matches Cluster 1's own independent finding that this exact shape was "the single most common in this batch"). CLIENT 241 -> 263 (smaller delta, consistent with tonight's Bucket A/B work already having covered most client-side catches).

Cluster 1 (commit ca03cfb, verified live via wrangler-tail forced-failure tests + real HTTP checks) correctly found and fixed 23 real sites within its scope (golf handlers + handleV2Games), exceeding its own doc's stated 16 by finding the same comment-only pattern independently, in the same session, before this correction was even applied here. That's real, already-verified, already-shipped work -- not affected by this correction.

What IS affected: the "34 remaining, unclustered" figure from the prior entry. Real corrected remaining count is closer to ~95 (118 total - 23 done in Cluster 1), not 34. Any future cluster-sizing for this sweep should re-derive the full precise list fresh against the corrected comment-exclusive empty-catch definition, not reuse the original 50-based list.
